title: Draws and resigning
line: Repetition, too little to mate, the fifty-move rule, agreement, and giving up a lost game.

steps.text: Black is far ahead and will mate you soon. But the black king is open. Check it with your queen from the edge of the board.
steps.hint: The queen goes to the edge, on the king's file.
steps.after: The king's only square is back beside it.

steps.text: Keep checking. Watch the king go back and forth until the same position comes up three times, with the same side to move.
That position has now come up three times with the same side to move. The game is over: a draw by repetition.
Two more draws: both players can agree to a draw, and after fifty moves by each side with no capture and no pawn move, it is a draw.
A player who sees that the game is lost may resign: give up, and the other side wins at once. You never have to resign.
A king and one bishop, or a king and one knight, can never mate a lone king. When neither side has enough left to mate, it is a draw.
If your time runs out, you lose, unless the other side cannot mate. Capture Black's last pawn: king and bishop cannot mate a lone king.
steps.hint: Your king can take the pawn before it reaches the last rank.
steps.after: Black has only a king and a bishop left. The game is a draw.

summary: A game is drawn by repetition, too little left to mate, fifty moves with no capture or pawn move, or agreement.
